Try the example

How to use the Bible quiz

Try answering before opening the explanation. Then read the referenced passage in your Bible. The aim is not only to remember a name or event, but to place it in the surrounding story.

Three questions to begin

Who built the ark at God’s instruction?

Noah. Genesis 6:14-22.

Which brother was to speak alongside Moses?

Aaron. Exodus 4:14-16.

Who cared for the injured traveller in Jesus’ parable?

The Samaritan. Luke 10:30-35.

Six games in Chrust

  • Word search: find biblical names and ideas in a letter grid.
  • Crossword: recall words from clues and check their intersections.
  • Blitz: answer Bible questions against a timer.
  • Match pairs: connect related items.
  • Build a verse: put the words back in order.
  • Where is this verse?: identify the source of a biblical passage.

Let the game lead back to reading

When an answer surprises you, return to the chapter. Write down one question for your next reading or discuss it with someone else. Trivia can help you recall Scripture, but it does not replace studying the text.
